articles.title: The seven best blenders in the US: for smoothies, frozen drinks and more
articles.summary: A great blender is a kitchen workhouse – I tested more than a dozen options including the Vitamix and Breville for budget, size, mulch factor, speed and whether they had plastic or glass jars. In the UK? Check out Filter UK’s top-rated blenders here.
body: There are few breakfasts that feel as healthy and refreshing as the ever-mutable smoothie. You can make them virtuous, with lots of greens and nut milk, or luscious, with full-fat dairy and cocoa powder – but in order to make a good one, you need a really good blender.

And while smoothies are the classic use for a blender, these appliances can do so much more; a truly great blender is a kitchen workhorse that can make your morning smoothie, your afternoon dip, your evening soup and even a frozen drink if you’re feeling frisky.

While blender technology has definitely improved in the last few decades – we now have high-speed contraptions that can make peanut butter in less than a minute – they’re all basically attempting to turn large pieces of food into a smoother result. If you’re looking for a new one, we’ve tested the best in the business.

articles.title: Daniel Roseberry adds ‘aerodynamic‘ edge to Schiaparelli’s surrealist glamour at Paris show
articles.summary: American in Paris showcases new simplicity with stretch cocktail frocks, but there’s still plenty of gold-foiled nipples and peekaboo fabrics to wow the frow. In a world of mega brands, the house of Schiaparelli is small but perfectly formed.
body: However, the Schiaparelli name punches above its weight. An exhibition at London’s V&A museum this year made a strong case for its founder, Elsa Schiaparelli, who collaborated with Salvador Dali and Jean Cocteau, as a creative force in the surrealism movement of the 1930s.

Kylie Jenner in a dress adorned with a fake lion’s head and Bella Hadid on the Cannes red carpet with an elaborate gold necklace covering her breasts have put the brand name all over TikTok. “It’s an amazing time at Schiap,” designer Daniel Roseberry said after his Paris show. “It’s a smaller house, but I feel like the voice is so big. It’s exclusive, but it’s real, because what we show on the catwalk is exactly what we sell.”

Schiap – Elsa’s nickname has become a nickname for her house – is strong meat. In his haute couture collections, Roseberry has leaned into Schiaparelli’s visual signature of anatomical detail parlayed into glamour. A tight dress might have a padded spine, gloves embroidered with glossy red fingernails, a jacket buttoned with a row of tiny gold ears or noses.
points: American in Paris showcases new simplicity with stretch cocktail frocks, but there’s still plenty of gold-foiled nipples and peekaboo fabrics to wow the frow.

articles.title: They’re delicious, popular and versatile – but how healthy are berries?
articles.summary: Experts say that if you’re eating any berry – strawberries, blackberries, currants, raspberries, blueberries – you are benefiting. Sprinkled on top of yoghurt, blended into smoothies or baked into crumbles, berries are among Americans’ favorite fruits.
body: Luckily, berries are as healthy as they are delicious and versatile: low in calories, full of vitamins and antioxidants, and a good source of fiber. Research shows that, depending on the type, berries support cardiovascular health, may boost gut health and fight inflammation and show promise as part of a “healthy dietary strategy for diabetes prevention and management”, to quote researchers. Meta-analyses also link compounds in berries with improved cognitive health.
“Berries’ high polyphenol content is what we think makes them so protective” when it comes to mental processes such as memory and attention, said Maggie Moon, a registered dietitian.

Polyphenols are a broad category of plant compounds; in berries, the most active and proportionally meaningful of them are anthocyanins, which also give many berries their blue, purple and red pigments.

Researchers are investigating whether berry polyphenols and the metabolites produced when gut microbes process them may influence inflammation and blood-vessel function. Because the brain depends on an extensive blood supply, better vascular function is one plausible route by which berries could support cognition.
points: Experts say that if you’re eating any berry – strawberries, blackberries, currants, raspberries, blueberries – you are benefiting.
Sprinkled on top of yoghurt, blended into smoothies or baked into crumbles, berries are among Americans’ favorite fruits.

articles.title: Brimful of personality: the rise of fashion’s ‘silly little hats’
articles.summary: From pillboxes and boaters to bicornes and buckets, characterful hats are making their way from the catwalk to the high street. “Here goes – an order for a million hats,” wrote Jackie Kennedy to Bergdorf Goodman before moving into the White House in the early 1960s.
body: This season at the turbo-high-end brand Loro Piana, whose clothes are beloved by tech bros and Kendall Roy, almost every model was wearing a hat. At Thom Browne, straw boaters came shrouded in colourful mesh. At Chloé there were see-through hats to match see-through trenchcoats and white sailor hats atop all-white outfits. Courrège’s hats were space-age, Burberry had big buckets, Bottega Veneta had hats brimming with charisma.

Some are calling them “personality hats”, others, affectionately, “silly little hats”, but hats that foreground character over practicality are enjoying time spent on heads from Milan fashion week to the shops. It’s not about a sou’wester in a storm but a creative punctuation point to an outfit, meant to draw the eye upwards.

Hats are a great expression of personality. According to David Long, the author of The Hats That Made Britain: A History of the Nation Through Its Headwear: “Excluding beanies and baseballs, hats are a rare opportunity for display, so I think the wearers are trying to say: ‘I’m not like everyone else, even though we all wear the same clothes nowadays.’ They’re showing off, in other words, but only a little bit.”
points: From pillboxes and boaters to bicornes and buckets, characterful hats are making their way from the catwalk to the high street.

articles.title: Chicken Scarpariello
articles.summary: Crispy-skinned chicken thighs, sweet Italian sausage, and roasted potatoes meet a punchy, vinegary pan sauce.
body: Chicken scarpariello (shoemaker’s chicken) brings together crispy-skinned chicken thighs and Italian sausage in a punchy sweet-and-sour pan sauce. This version gets its tang from white wine vinegar and pickled Peppadew peppers, which mingle with onions, fresh bell pepper, garlic, rosemary, and all the savory drippings left behind by the meat.

While some chicken scarpariello recipes cook potatoes right in the pan, we roast fingerlings separately so they stay crisp—perfect for dragging through all that vinegary sauce. Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs are the move here: They brown beautifully, stay juicy as they braise, and add plenty of flavor to the sauce.

Peppadews add sweetness and a mild tang, but hot cherry peppers or pepperoncini work too if you want something sharper or spicier. Serve the scarpariello straight from the skillet for a hearty dinner that lands somewhere between weeknight comfort food and Sunday supper.
points: Crispy-skinned chicken thighs, sweet Italian sausage, and roasted potatoes meet a punchy, vinegary pan sauce.

articles.title: On the Podcast: Julian Klausner on Designing His Best Dries Van Noten Collection Yet
articles.summary: About 48 hours ago in Paris, Julian Klausner presented his spring 2027 Dries Van Noten ready-to-wear collection. For this Friday’s episode of “The Run-Through,” Nicole meets Klausner in the Vogue France offices to discuss the inspiration behind the show, his journey to Dries, and his industry peers.
body: “Yesterday, a friend of mine said that she saw it as ‘movie star meets picking up the kids,’” Kausner says, descibing the sensibility of the latest Dries collection. “I like to imagine what Marilyn Monroe would be looking like today if she had to run errands after a day of filming.”

Asked about the label’s ethos more broadly, Klausner says: “I think the playfulness and the invitation to be a little bit extra with your clothes is very much what we stand for.” He spends a lot of time in the archives, but he also sees Dries’s history walking around every day. “We have a lot of colleagues that have been there for decades,” he tells Nicole. “People are constantly wearing pieces from the ’90s or 2000s.”

Also on today’s episode: producer Chelsea Daniel catches up with Chloe for a quick fit check and to talk about the shows she’s attended since arriving in Paris; they speak to Jordan Roth after Schiaparelli; and we hear from the Chloé show’s hairstylist.
points: About 48 hours ago in Paris, Julian Klausner presented his spring 2027 Dries Van Noten ready-to-wear collection.

articles.title: Changing This Setting May Extend Your Battery Life on iOS 27
articles.summary: If you've updated your iPhone to iOS 27, you might have already put Siri AI to the test or tried out some of Apple's AI-powered photo editing features. But you may have also noticed something else: Your iPhone's battery isn't lasting as long between charges.
body: Technically, this feature isn't new. Before iOS 27, Apple called it "Wi-Fi Assist," but it worked a bit differently. In iOS 26, Wi-Fi Assist simply switches over to cellular when your wifi signal is too weak. With iOS 27's Connectivity Assist, it seems your iPhone can tap into both networks at the same time. If so, that may play some role in why this rejiggered feature seems to be dragging down people's batteries more than it used to.

There's another new addition with Connectivity Assist that could also be part of the problem: Unlike Wi-Fi Assist, Connectivity Assist sends DNS requests over cellular data, which can bypass the rules that ad blockers put in place to stop pop-ups from making their way into your iPhone. As such, even Apple recommends that you disable Connectivity Assist if you use an ad blocker. So, if your iPhone is constantly sending out DNS requests while on cellular data, bypassing your active ad blockers, that could be putting extra strain on your battery, too.

articles.title: Léa Seydoux on ‘The Unknown,’ Beauty, Fame, and Acting
articles.summary: Léa Seydoux talks Arthur Harari’s “The Unknown,” her approach to acting, and why she’s drawn to films about identity, mystery, and the unknowable.
body: Recently, Léa Seydoux was in a bathroom in New York when a woman—“very American, face full of makeup”—approached her with the nagging feeling that they had met before.
“I feel like I know you,” Seydoux remembers her saying, briefly slipping into a nasal American accent. “I’ve seen you somewhere.”

Seydoux, who has spent nearly two decades appearing in some of the world’s biggest films (including installments in the Mission: Impossible, James Bond, and Dune franchises), didn’t rush to solve the mystery for her. “I was like, ‘Really?’” she recalls, clearly amused by the encounter. After scrutinizing Seydoux’s face, the woman eventually decided that she simply reminded her of somebody she knew. “She couldn’t really place me.”

It’s an apt anecdote for Seydoux to relay while discussing The Unknown, Arthur Harari’s eerie, shape-shifting new film that premiered in May at Cannes, played at the Toronto International Film Festival last month, and is currently screening as part of the New York Film Festival.

articles.title: The Holei Sea Arch, a Centuries-Old Hawaii Wonder, Crumbles Into the Pacific
articles.summary: A tropical storm was moving through the area when the 90-foot lava rock formation disintegrated, the National Park Service said.
body: For more than half a millennium, one of Hawaii’s most cherished geological marvels, an arch 90 feet high composed of lava rock, withstood a battering from the Pacific and evoked a sense of awe.

But that formation, the Holei Sea Arch at Hawai’i Volcanoes National Park, is now gone from the coastline on the Big Island, having crumbled into the ocean around the same time as a tropical storm brought strong winds and heavy rain to Hawaii in late September, the National Park Service said on Thursday.
A cascade of tributes and vacation photos quickly began pouring in from those who have hiked the park’s rugged coastline over the years, many of them lamenting the landmark’s demise.
The Park Service posted before-and-after photos of the coastline on social media on Thursday night, along with a crying face emoji.

articles.title: These 7 Stunning Airbnbs Sit Directly Inside of US National Parks
articles.summary: You can’t get much more convenient—or scenic—than these stays, from Yosemite to Acadia.
body: When you’re planning a national park trip, there are plenty of moving parts: what hikes to do, what to pack, where to stop, and how to squeeze the most out of your time. So why not make where you stay the easiest (and most scenic) part? The right home base can change the whole essence of a US national park trip, trading an early-morning, hours-long drive for coffee with a mountain view, access to a trail practically outside your door, and more time in the wild. A stay directly inside the park means skipping the morning entrance line and avoiding long pre- and post-hike drives.

There’s something wonderfully immersive about waking up inside a national park. Imagine stepping outside to your patio as mist lifts off the peaks of the Great Smoky Mountains, watching ripples cross a glassy pond in Glacier, or opening the door of a Yosemite cabin to views framed by towering pines. From Rocky Mountain ’s rugged peaks to Acadia ’s rocky coastline, these bucket-list-worthy Airbnbs make the parks feel more attainable—and have some of the most jaw-dropping views of them all.
